newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus partners, Alenia in China plane talks.
newsitem.headline: Airbus partners, Alenia in China plane talks.

text.p: The four Airbus partners and Italy's Alenia are in discussions on how to bring a planned 100-seat passenger jet to be built in China can be brought within the Airbus structure, an Aerospatiale spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
"The Airbus members and Alenia have started discussions on defining a structure to manage the programme within the Airbus system," the spokeswoman said.

Aviation Industries of China (AVIC), which will hold 46 percent of the project, has asked its European partners in the AIA joint venture to bring Airbus Industrie into the Asian Express-100 programme. Aerospatiale is an AIA member.

The European partners will discuss how development and production for the AE-100 will be shared out among the Western firms. This will then decide what percentages they will get in the programme, the spokeswoman said.
"We are discussing the best structure to meet the wishes of AVIC," she said. Nothing had been finalised yet and no percentages had been fixed for the European firms, she added.
The Aero International Asia joint venture comprises Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc and Alenia, a unit of Finmeccanica.
AIA will take 39 percent of the AE-100 project and Singapore Technologies Aerospace 15 percent, AVIC has said.

An Airbus spokesman said a separate Airbus subsidiary could be set up for the 100-seater, which would have strong common elements with the Airbus product range and draw on Airbus management and marketing.
If the AE-100 were to brought into the Airbus structure, Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa) would have a role in the programme as it is a senior Airbus partner along with Aerospatiale.

Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
